name: Canopus
tagline: The second-brightest star in the night sky — a southern beacon used to steer spacecraft.
history: Canopus outshines every star but Sirius — and only its 310-light-year distance hides a luminosity over ten thousand Suns. So reliably bright and far south, it became the celestial reference for spacecraft guidance: star trackers on Voyager, Galileo and deep-space probes lock onto it to hold their orientation. Named for the pilot of Menelaus's ship in myth, it is invisible from most of Europe but rules southern skies.
